nodes.label: Breeds: from 2 kg to over 70 kg

dog.caption: One species, a huge range of sizes. The model stands for a medium, athletic breed; the body plan is the same in all.

dog_skeleton.caption: Dog and human side by side. The dog figures are from the vertebral formula in the open-access paper cited on this card and the 13 rib pairs on the Ribs card; the human figures are on the human cards linked above. The cervical count is 7 in both.

dog_ear.caption: Range of hearing from the Hearing range reference. Dogs hear much higher sounds than people but lose out at the very low end.

dog_teeth.caption: Adult teeth: a dog has 42 (2 x (I3/3, C1/1, P4/4, M2/3), dvm360); people have 32.

bars.label: dog resting heart rate, low (per min)

dog_heart.caption: Typical resting ranges: dog 70-120 per minute (Merck Veterinary Manual), human 60-100 per minute (human heart card). Small dogs are near the top of the dog range.

dog_retina.caption: Beagle retina (Mol Vis 2008): about 23 rods for each cone at the sharpest spot and about 41 at the lower edge. Cone types: dog 2, human 3.

dog_turb_olf.ylabel: area in cm² or number of genes
dog_turb_olf.caption: Approximate comparison: lining area from the Olfaction reference (dog about 170 cm², human about 10 cm²) and receptor gene counts from the receptor-gene comparison of Quignon et al. 2003 and Wikipedia (about 800 and about 400).
